assumptions: THIS INCREMENT CHANGES NO DECISION AND NO CODE. It removes one spent blocker and rewrites two whose STATED REASON went false while their conclusion stayed true. That distinction is the whole of this increment: the conclusion "tenant isolation is not proven" still holds, and every reason this manifest gave for it has been superseded.

SPENT, THEREFORE REMOVED: the blocker saying RFC-2026-017 was Proposed and that no role is created and no policy written until it was disposed. That record was disposed on 2026-09-05 and db/foundation/migrations/001_service_roles.sql creates app_worker, app_command and app_maintenance on main. The work the blocker forbade has shipped.

REWRITTEN, NOT REMOVED -- "No tenant table exists". False from batch 010 onward: 45 tables are created across 010_identity.sql to 140_audit.sql and make db-rls-smoke runs 554 isolation cases against them. What survives is narrower and harder to state: RFC-2026-017 §7's negative -- the service identity refused an operation the §8 matrix marks N for service, with an error rather than an empty result -- is still undischarged, and RFC-2026-022 §5/8 gives the measurement that explains why. The only member of app_worker is postgres, which holds rolbypassrls, so a refusal observed today attributes to an absent grant rather than to a policy.

REWRITTEN, NOT REMOVED -- "the negative assertion does not exist". It does: 116 cases in tests/db/identity/isolation-cases.mjs have an id beginning `service`, and batch 070's header calls its four `service-cannot-*` INSERT cases the policy-layer denials that flip when a service identity exists. So the assertion is written and its SUBJECT is missing. The debt also changed hands: it was recorded as owed by whoever writes the first tenant table, and it is owed by the RFC that creates a worker.

amends_without_owning IS EMPTIED. It carried four paths from this package's earlier increment and this branch touches none of them; verify-branch-scope refuses a declaration explaining nothing the branch changed. All four are named in the manifest's new rationale.

STATUS IS DELIBERATELY NOT MOVED: this package stays in_progress. An Author may move work only as far as in_review, and moving it would be a claim about completeness rather than the correction of a false sentence.

security_privacy_cost_impact: None to the code. The privacy-relevant point is what the manifest now SAYS: it no longer implies that no tenant table exists, which a reader could take as meaning there is nothing yet to isolate. There are 45 tables and the isolation of the service path is still unproven, and those two facts are now in the same sentence.
known_limitations: NOTHING PREVENTS THE NEXT STALE SENTENCE. A blocker list is prose and no lint reads English.

THE TWO REWRITTEN BLOCKERS NOW CITE COUNTS -- 45 tables, 554 cases, 116 service cases -- AND A COUNT IN PROSE IS THE EXACT THING THIS REPOSITORY HAS WATCHED GO STALE five times. They are written as facts about a measurement taken on a named revision rather than as standing properties, which is the best a sentence can do; a batch that adds a table makes them understatements rather than falsehoods, which is the safe direction.

A rule tying a blocker that names a decision record to that record's status, if one can be written without reading prose.
